criteria.reasoning: The report explicitly identifies the subject as “Robert Frederick (‘Robert F.’) Smith, founder, chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners” and distinguishes him from the musician and former senator with the same name. The biographical, philanthropic, wealth, and legal details are presented as belonging to the Vista executive, with no apparent merged or misattributed record.
The report identifies Smith as “Founder, Chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners” and says Vista Equity Partners is “which he founded in 2000.” This satisfies the required roles and founding year.

The report states, “B.S. in chemical engineering, Cornell University (1985); M.B.A., Columbia Business School (1994).” This gives the required Cornell chemical engineering degree and the correct schools and years for both degrees.
The report states under “Personal and professional background” that Smith’s “Residence: Austin, Texas.” This directly satisfies the criterion.
The report states, “Net worth: about $10 billion,” identifying it as Forbes' real-time figure for March 8, 2026. This is within the required $9 billion–$13 billion range.

The report identifies “Fund II Foundation, his private foundation” and says Smith “is its founding director and President”; it also describes the foundation as his giving vehicle and notes recent 990-PFs list him as a director. This meets the criterion’s required identification and attribution.

The report states that in 2016 Cornell received a “$50 million (combined, Smith and Fund II Foundation)” gift. It also says Cornell named the “Robert Frederick Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering,” satisfying the required amount and naming recognition.

The report says, “At the May 19, 2019 commencement he pledged to pay off the student loans of about 400 graduates,” and gives the amount as “$34 million.” This matches the required year, occasion, student loans, and final gift amount.

The report describes SFI as an “Income-contingent alternative” for “STEM juniors and seniors at HBCUs” and states “$50 million from Fund II Foundation” plus a “$50 million personal gift from Smith.” It also correctly says Cisco’s and Steinbridge Group’s commitments came from those firms, not Smith.

The report states that Prairie View A&M University was one of SFI's first nine partner HBCUs, announced in November 2020, and that it remains listed as an SFI partner school. This is a documented connection between SFI and a Texas HBCU specified by the criterion.

The report says, “Fund II Foundation's only Texas HBCU grant is a $10,000 donation to Prairie View A&M in 2021,” and describes Prairie View A&M and other Texas schools only as SFI partner schools. It mentions Smith’s Huston-Tillotson commencement address, not a gift, and does not claim any other Texas HBCU gift or named fund.

The report says, “On October 15, 2020 the DOJ announced that Smith had entered a non-prosecution agreement” concerning an offshore scheme to hide income. It gives the payment as “more than $139 million in taxes and penalties (about $56 million plus $82 million),” satisfying the criterion.

The report states that Smith “entered a non-prosecution agreement” and “was not charged,” and that “He admitted the conduct.” It does not say he was indicted, convicted, pleaded guilty, sentenced, or cleared, nor attribute Brockman’s case to him.

The report says, “Do not raise the matter with Smith or his staff, and keep it out of proposals and talking points.” It recommends internal review and a neutral response if Smith raises it, which the criterion explicitly allows.

The report estimates single-gift capacity at “$25–50 million” and recommends an “Ask: $10 million over five years.” Both are stated as dollar figures, and the ask does not exceed the capacity estimate’s upper end of $50 million.

The report’s factual claims align with the fact sheet, including the $10 billion net-worth figure, the documented gift amounts, the Texas HBCU connections, and the DOJ matter. Its $25 million figure for Cornell’s 2022 gift is explicitly allowed as a source-disagreement item in section 8.
